dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: yasya kasyendriyasyāpi vyāghātāc ca nirodhataḥ | praviṣṭasyādvaye śūnye tatraivātmā prakāśate ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: When any sense, whichever it is, is obstructed (by something striking it from outside) or deliberately blocked, one enters the non-dual void, and right there the Self shines.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: when a sense is obstructed by an external cause, naturally, or by a self-imposed device, it cannot contact the world, a feeling of emptiness arises in it, the mind turns inward and is absorbed in a void without subject-object duality, where the Self is revealed. Bäumer reads vyāghāta as obstruction 'by striking (an external object)'.
dharana.technique_name: When a Sense Is Blocked, the Void Behind It
dharana.instruction: Gently block one sense, such as covering the ears, and rest in the empty space that opens.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 89 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the gentle block (palms over the ears)
the empty space where the sense had been reaching out
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is one sense going quiet, and the empty, inward space that appears where it used to reach outward.
geometry.svg_hint: an ear outline with a soft barrier in front of it and an open space behind it
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Sense goes quiet
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a sense that is always reaching outward goes quiet, and attention falls into the space behind it. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Gently quiet one sense and turn toward the space that opens
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The empty space that appears when one sense is gently blocked

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: When any sense, whichever it is, is obstructed (by something striking it from outside) or deliberately blocked, one enters the non-dual void, and right there the Self shines.
adiyogi.method_summary: Gently block one sense: rest the palms lightly over the ears, or use earplugs, or simply close the eyes. Notice the emptiness that appears where the sense was reaching out, and rest in that space. Also notice such moments when they happen by themselves, such as a sudden silence.

honesty.disclosure: Door 066 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 66 (verse 89) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Use only gentle blocks: palms resting lightly on the ears, earplugs, or closed eyes. Never press on the eyes or ears, and never block the nose or mouth. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
